=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
principles:
  typescript:
    strict_mode: true
    target: ES2022
    no_any: "Avoid `any` — use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generics"
    async_first: "All DB calls, LLM calls, and I/O are async — always await"

  error_handling:
    pattern: "AppError class hierarchy with immutable HTTP status codes"
    subclasses: [ValidationError 400, AuthError 401, ForbiddenError 403, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, UnprocessableError 422]
    serialization: "{ error: string, code?: string, details?: Record<string, unknown> }"
    rule: "Throw from route handlers; centralized errorHandler middleware catches and serializes"

  database:
    driver: "pg Pool (async, connection pooling)"
    helpers: "query<T>() returns T[], queryOne<T>() returns T|undefined, execute() returns { rowCount }"
    placeholders: "$1, $2, ... (numbered, NOT positional ?)"
    transactions: "transaction<T>(fn) wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK"
    migrations: "SQL files in pg-migrations/, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files, tracked in schema_migrations"
    slow_query_logging: "Queries > 500ms logged with sanitized params"

  validation:
    library: zod
    pattern: "Middleware factories — validateBody(schema), validateQuery(schema), validateParams(schema)"
    method: "safeParse (not .parse() which throws)"
    response: "{ error: firstIssueMessage, details: zodError.issues }"

  llm:
    return_type: "ChatResult { text: string, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens } }"
    rule: "Always use .text accessor — never treat ChatResult as a string"
    providers: "Multi-provider routing via model registry — claude-cli, anthropic, openai-compat, openrouter"

  api_design:
    documentation: "JSDoc @swagger annotations on every route → auto-generated OpenAPI spec"
    pagination: "{ items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }"
    response_shape: "Success: res.json(data). Error: { error, code, details } via AppError"
    middleware_chain: "validateBody(schema) → authRequired → async handler"
    security_headers: "helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, noSniff, referrerPolicy)"
    caching: "Cache-Control: no-store on all responses, etag: false"

  testing:
    backend: "Jest with ts-jest, serial (maxWorkers: 1), 30s timeout, PG_POOL_SIZE=1"
    frontend: "Vitest with jsdom, globals: true"
    rule: "Always clean up DB pool connections in afterAll()"

  code_style:
    no_over_engineering: "Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly necessary"
    no_premature_abstraction: "Three similar lines > premature helper function"
    minimal_containers: "Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't change"
    security_first: "Never commit .env files, API keys, or secrets. Use vault for sensitive values."

=== PROJECT CONTEXT (L3) ===
name: rorca
type: web-app
purpose: AI spec orchestration platform that converts plain-English briefs into structured user story specs and autonomously executes them story-by-story via isolated agent subprocesses (claude, opencode, or codex)

stack:
  - React 18
  - TypeScript 5.7 (strict)
  - Vite 5
  - Tailwind CSS 3
  - xterm.js (@xterm/xterm)
  - react-router-dom 7
  - framer-motion
  - recharts
  - Express.js
  - PostgreSQL 16 (pg pool, pgvector, Apache AGE)
  - pg-boss (job queue)
  - Node.js >= 20
  - tsx (TypeScript runner)
  - Jest (backend tests)
  - Vitest (frontend tests)
  - Playwright (E2E)

key_modules:
  - src/panels/ — 5 primary UI panels (Specs, Runs, Analytics, Direction, Settings)
  - src/components/ — shared UI (Sidebar, RunTerminal, CommandPalette, slide-overs)
  - src/contexts/ — WorkspaceContext, AuthContext, ThemeContext, ToastContext
  - backend/src/routes/ — 32 Express route files
  - backend/src/lib/ — core services (sse-hub, direction-stack, llm-client, execution-engine, context-router, workspace-echolocation, rate-limiter, scheduler)
  - backend/src/worker.ts — pg-boss worker process (pipeline job consumer)
  - backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts — sole execution engine for all agent types
  - backend/src/db/ — PostgreSQL pool, migration runner, 70+ migrations
  - backend/src/mcp/ — MCP stdio server (24 tools)
  - forge/ — spec JSON files, run-loop.sh bash fallback, self-register script

constraints:
  - Migrations must use timestamp format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files (sequential 001-079 already exist)
  - Worker process must be running for pipeline triggers to execute
  - AGE search_path must be restored after every graph query
  - Auth middleware is globally disabled (intentional, local tool)
  - CLAUDE_BIN full path required for child process spawning (NVM PATH not inherited)
  - spec id is always the filename slug, never the human title

deployment_target: local (self-hosted, npm run dev) or Docker Compose

ports:
  frontend: 5210
  backend: 3030
  finops_sim: 5200

integrations:
  - claude CLI (claude --print)
  - opencode CLI (opencode run)
  - codex CLI (codex --approval-mode auto-edit)
  - GitHub OAuth + webhooks
  - Linear (post-launch)
  - Vercel (post-launch)
  - Slack (post-launch)
  - Stripe billing

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Build a comprehensive `rorca_recall` MCP tool that composes the entire Rorca PostgreSQL brain into a single callable tool for CLI sessions. This is the "inject the brain" command — one MCP call that returns everything an AI agent needs to work on a workspace with full context.

## What it must return (single JSON payload):

1. **Synthesized Direction Stack** (L1–L5) — the full merged direction string exactly as the execution engine sees it, via `synthesizeDirectionStack()` from `direction-stack.ts` which uses the 3-tier memory-router retrieval chain (CAG cache → RAG search → Graph)

2. **Memory entries** — all active memories from the `memories` PostgreSQL table for the workspace, filtered by `deleted_at IS NULL`, ordered by pinned DESC then created_at DESC. Include category, content, confidence, source_type, related_files, pinned status. Support optional category filter param.

3. **Workspace health** — echolocation report from `workspace-echolocation.ts`: health score (0-100), detected stack (frameworks, languages, tools), context file status (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, .rorca/config.json existence + line counts), monorepo detection, actionable suggestions.

4. **Recent pipeline runs** — last 5 runs from `pipeline_runs` table with status, spec_path, started_at, finished_at, agent_type, model, total tokens/cost. For each run, include aggregated story_results (pass/fail/skip counts, pass rate).

5. **Installed skills** — all skill files from `.rorca/skills/` directory with name and content preview (first 200 chars).

6. **Workspace context** — cached schema_snapshot and git_memory from `workspace_context` table (the hydrated DB schema and git history summary).

7. **Workspace metadata** — id, label, path, domains, created_at from `workspaces` table.

8. **Active/queued runs** — any currently running or queued pipeline runs with their story progress.

## Architecture (API-first, MCP-second):

### Backend route: `GET /api/recall?workspaceId=X`
- New Express route file `backend/src/routes/recall.ts`
- Composes all 8 data sources server-side using parallel `Promise.all()` for independent queries
- Returns structured JSON with clear sections
- Token budget estimation on the response (chars/4)
- Swagger `@swagger` JSDoc annotations for OpenAPI auto-generation → MCP auto-discovery
- Uses existing query helpers (`query`, `queryOne` from `db/index.ts`)
- Uses existing libs: `synthesizeDirectionStack()`, `echolocate()`, context-cache helpers
- Mounted in `server.ts` at `/api/recall`

### MCP tool: `rorca_recall` in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts`
- Registered with `server.registerTool()` following existing patterns (wrapToolCall, fetchWithRetry, timedFetch)
- Added to `IDEMPOTENT_TOOLS` set (safe to retry, GET-equivalent)
- Cache key: `recall:${workspaceId}`
- Input schema: `workspaceId` (required), `category` (optional memory filter), `includeRuns` (optional, default true), `includeHealth` (optional, default true), `storyText` (optional, for semantic memory retrieval)
- Output: structured JSON with all 8 sections + meta (totalTokens, latencyMs, retrievalTier)
- Description emphasizes this is the "brain dump" tool for injecting full workspace context into any AI session

### MCP prompt: `recall` registered via `server.registerPrompt()`
- Slash-command shorthand for invoking the tool
- Prompt text instructs the LLM to call `rorca_recall` and use the returned context

## Quality requirements:
- Must handle missing workspace gracefully (404 with helpful error)
- Must handle partial failures (if echolocation fails, still return direction + memories)
- Response must include `meta.totalTokens` estimate so callers know context budget impact
- All DB queries use `$1, $2` numbered placeholders (not `?`)
- Backend type-checks clean (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- Tests: Jest integration tests for the recall route covering happy path, missing workspace, partial data scenarios
